usageNotes: Sends an ACPI shutdown signal to a remote QEMU VM — equivalent to pressing the power button, allowing the guest OS to shut down gracefully. Returns a remote UPID that must be polled to confirm completion; the call returns immediately and does not wait for the guest to finish shutting down. Requires Resource.Manage privilege on the remote+vmid combination; the VM must be in a running state on the target PVE remote.

examples.summary: Gracefully shut down VM 105 on the prod-hetzner remote

destructiveReason: Initiates a guest OS shutdown, which stops all running services and workloads on the VM; if the guest ignores the ACPI signal or hangs, the VM remains in a transitional state until manually killed.
tips: Poll the returned UPID via the task-status endpoint to determine when the shutdown has actually completed before taking follow-up actions (migrate, snapshot, etc.).
The 'node' body param is optional — omit it to let PDM resolve the node automatically, or supply it to target a specific PVE cluster node when the VM could be on multiple nodes.
This sends an ACPI signal (graceful); use the stop endpoint instead if the guest is unresponsive and you need a hard power-off.
Token-based auth is supported (allowtoken: true), making this safe to call from automation without interactive credentials.
